title: Go SDK: Response envelope & validation pipeline with generics and streaming transforms
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Consumers need a consistent, type-safe way to decode structured responses from streaming and non-streaming endpoints. Current helpers use ad-hoc maps or reflection in some call sites which leads to runtime errors, poor ergonomics for streaming transformations, and duplication across example code.

Goal: Implement a lightweight 'Envelope' pattern + generics-based decode helpers for the Go SDK that: (1) provide compile-time typed accessors for the payload, (2) support streaming transforms (unwrapping envelopes mid-stream without buffering entire payloads), (3) integrate with existing retry middleware and deadline semantics, and (4) ship with examples and migration notes.

Scope: library-level API changes (non-breaking surface for most users), new helpers in internal/streaming and public pkg rwsdk/v2/typed, unit and integration tests, benchmarks, and docs. Backwards compatibility: keep existing unmarshal helpers but mark legacy reflect-based functions as deprecated with migration guide.
acceptance_criteria: Public API: Add Envelope[T any] generic type with metadata and typed Body() accessor documented in SDK reference.

Streaming: Implement StreamUnwrapper that can decode a sequence of Envelope[T] from a json.Decoder without materializing large bodies; example that streams 1000 small envelopes with <5% memory overhead compared to current approach.

Validation: Pluggable validator interface so teams can plug schema checks (JSON Schema or custom) that run after typed decode; validation errors surface with stable error types for retries to inspect.

Retry integration: Deadline-aware middleware can inspect validation errors and choose to retry only idempotent requests; add tests that simulate transient validation failures and ensure policy triggers correctly.
Docs & examples: One end-to-end example in examples/typed-envelopes demonstrating streaming chat response decoding and structured function-calling output parsing.

Benchmarks: Microbenchmarks showing decode latency overhead <= 5% vs current fastest decode path for small payloads and <= 10% for large streaming bodies while reducing peak memory by >= 30% for stream-heavy workloads.
Migration: Add migration guide and deprecation notes; existing code paths continue to work by default.

Tests: Unit tests cover generics instantiation, unknown-field fallback, validator plugin, and error wrapping for retry decisions. Integration tests exercise SDK send/receive with dedicated runtime container in CI.
tasks: Design API sketch and propose Envelope[T any] shape (include metadata, status, raw bytes access) - owner: Luca
Implement Envelope and Body() typed accessor + JSON tags and custom Unmarshal for edge cases
Implement StreamUnwrapper using json.Decoder token stream to decode envelopes incrementally
Create Validator interface and default JSONSchema adapter (can be a wrapper around github.com/santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema)
Integrate validation step into decode helpers with opt-in behavior (default: off)
Wire decode helpers into SDK streaming client path and add retry hooks to surface validation errors
Write unit tests, property tests for unknown fields fallback, and fuzz decode for safety
Add benchmarks and CI job to collect baseline numbers
Author examples and migration doc; update CHANGELOG and deprecations.md
Code review, address feedback, merge, and cut release sdk-go-2.3
comments: 2025-02-15 Maya Chen: Spiked a couple prototypes. Using encoding/json.Decoder with Token allows us to decode small envelopes as they arrive. Initial concern: big 'data' fields still cause allocation when mapped into structs. Proposal: provide BodyRaw() to stream directly to io.Writer for large binary blobs.

2025-02-18 Samir Patel: Code review notes - avoid heavy reflection; prefer generics to produce ergonomic constructors. Also suggested adding an examples/streaming/perf harness to validate memory claims.
2025-02-20 Priya Gupta: UX feedback - callers will want a simple UnwrapStream[T](r io.Reader) -> <-chan Result[T] pattern. Keep both pull (DecodeNext) and push (channel) APIs for flexibility.

2025-02-23 Luca Martinez: Implemented initial Envelope[T] and StreamUnwrapper. Pushed branch feature/ENG-47011-envelope with small tests. See link to PR below. Key decision: when unknown fields are present, populate a 'RawExtras' map[string]json.RawMessage instead of failing; this keeps strict typed decode while preserving data for forward compatibility.

2025-02-26 Security review (note): KMS/HSM not impacted; payload validators run in process. No secret material extraction. We should run a short threat review if customers plug third-party validators. Marking security_review_required=false for now.

2025-02-28 QA: Integration test flake observed on CI when streaming >50 parallel connections. Root cause: global decoder pool contended. Switching to per-stream decoder instances improved stability. Added fix to branch and running benchmarks.

2025-03-03 Maya Chen: Addressed code-review feedback from Samir and Priya. Benchmarks show 35% lower peak RSS on streaming test vs reflect-based approach. Ready for final review and merge once docs are added.
